questions.question: What is a guarantee that another driver sees you?

options.text: Eye contact
Using a turn signal
Following another vehicle
Nothing

questions.explanation: Nothing guarantees that a driver sees you. Always assume that any vehicle that can enter your path will do so.

questions.question: How should a motorcyclist's cushion of space change?

options.text: It should always stay the same.
It should change based on riding conditions.
It is not necessary in most situations.
It should be avoided to keep traffic moving safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should change based on riding conditions.
questions.explanation: You need more space if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. Increase your distance if the road is slippery, you cannot see ahead, or traffic is heavy.

questions.question: What should you do to be more visible while riding?

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day.
Wear dark clothes.
Keep your headlight on at all times.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on at all times.
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright and reflective clothing, keep your headlight on at all times, and change your lane position as needed.

questions.question: What is the proper footwear for riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Shoes with long, loose laces.
Shoes with short heels.
Shoes with tall heels.
Always sneakers.

questions.explanation: Wear sturdy shoes that cover and support your ankles. Short heels are best because tall heels can catch on surfaces. Tuck in shoelaces so they do not get caught on anything.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular in shape?

options.text: School crossing sign
Railroad crossing sign
Stop sign
Speed limit sign

questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black text. These signs show the rules you must follow while driving.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a way to prevent a friend from driving while intoxicated?

options.text: Arrange a safe ride home for them.
Keep them busy with other activities so they drink slower and sober up.
Make them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving.
Ask other friends to help stop them from driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving.
questions.explanation: To stop someone from drinking and driving, arrange an alternative ride, keep them busy to slow their drinking, find excuses to keep them from leaving, and ask friends to help.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Avoid sudden moves.
Use both brakes.
Brake quickly.

questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce your speed, avoid sudden movements, and use both brakes gently.

questions.question: When riding at night, what should a motorcyclist NOT do compared to daytime riding?

options.text: Ride more slowly.
Allow more space between their motorcycle and other vehicles.
Use their high beam whenever possible.
Tailgate other vehicles.

questions.explanation: At night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther. Be flexible about your lane position.

questions.question: On a motorcycle with a sidecar, where should the passenger ride?

options.text: On the motorcycle seat.
In the sidecar.
Either on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.
Neither on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.

questions.explanation: The passenger should ride in the sidecar and keep their hands inside at all times.

questions.question: Which of the following provides the best protection for a rider?

options.text: Goggles
A face shield
A windshield
Eyeglasses

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield or eyeglasses do not provide the same protection.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings, what should you do?

options.text: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Grip the handlebars tightly and speed up to pass the hazard.
Ride in a zigzag pattern.
Move onto the shoulder instead of the grooves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Weaving on rain grooves or bridge gratings is not dangerous. Simply relax and ride straight across at a steady speed. Zigzagging is more dangerous than riding straight.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a safe way to prevent rider fatigue?

options.text: Protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain
Take artificial stimulants
Limit your riding to less distance per day
Take frequent breaks

questions.explanation: On long trips, take frequent breaks and do not ride more than six hours per day. Dress to protect yourself from the weather. Never use artificial stimulants because the effects can be dangerous when they wear off.

questions.question: When riding at night, what should you do?

options.text: Distances are easier to judge than during the day.
Using high beam headlights always makes it harder to see.
Use only one lane position.
Reduce your speed.

questions.explanation: When riding at night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use your high beam headlight when there is no other traffic. Be ready to change lane position if conditions change.

questions.question: When is it important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When you are tired while riding
When you will slow down where other drivers don't expect it
When there is a stop sign ahead
When your signals are not working

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down where other drivers don't expect it
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are hard to see compared to larger vehicles. Flash your brake light before slowing down in unexpected places, such as in the middle of a block or near an alley.

questions.question: When entering a curve, a group of motorcycles should:

options.text: Ride in single-file formation
Ride in staggered formation
Ride in pairs
Ride on the shoulder

questions.explanation: Although staggered formation is usually best, switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop your motorcycle quickly?

options.text: Use the front brake only
Use the rear brake first
Close the throttle and use the front brake
Use both brakes at the same time

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time. Press the brakes firmly and do not panic if they lock.

questions.question: Making eye contact with another driver:

options.text: Guarantees that the other driver will yield to you
Is not worth the effort
Does not mean the driver will yield to you
Means the driver knows you are there

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean the driver will yield to you
questions.explanation: Never assume that eye contact with a driver means they will properly yield to you.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When riding near stopped or slow-moving cars, a motorcyclist should:

options.text: Pull over and wait for traffic to move
Ride on the shoulder to pass quickly
Weave between cars to get through quickly
Not weave between cars

questions.explanation: Weaving between parked or slow cars is dangerous because of opening doors or cars pulling into traffic. You will not have room to safely maneuver. Never ride on the shoulder because other drivers will not expect you there.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle properly, you should:

options.text: Sit so you use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up
Sit far back on the seat so your arms are straight
Keep your knees away from the gas tank
Drag your feet on the ground

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so you use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up
questions.explanation: Sit so you use your arms to control the motorcycle, not to hold yourself up. Your arms should be slightly bent at the handlebars. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet on the footrests to help balance.

questions.question: What happens to steering if your front tire goes flat while riding?

options.text: The steering will feel heavy.
The steering will feel loose.
The steering will not change.
The ride will feel too smooth.

questions.explanation: A flat front tire makes steering feel heavy. If your steering feels heavy, leave the road right away and check your tires.

questions.question: As a beginning rider, what following distance should you keep behind another vehicle?

options.text: Keep at least four seconds of distance between you and the other vehicle.
Get as close as possible to the other vehicle.
Do not worry about following distance.
Always ride on the left side of the lane so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep at least four seconds of distance between you and the other vehicle.
questions.explanation: Beginning riders should keep at least four seconds between them and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if road or weather conditions are poor.

questions.question: What do most motorcycle crashes involve?

options.text: Speeds greater than 35 mph.
Worn tires.
Riding in the dark.
Riders with little experience on their motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders with little experience on their motorcycles.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen to riders who are new to their motorcycles.

questions.question: What should a motorcycle operator do when riding with a passenger?

options.text: Keep a longer distance from the vehicle ahead.
Ride faster.
Let air out of the tires to handle the extra weight.
Do not alert passengers to dangers ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a longer distance from the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: With a passenger on board, a motorcycle handles differently. You should keep more space between you and other vehicles.

questions.question: Why should motorcycle riders not rely only on mirrors?

options.text: Motorcycle mirrors are smaller than car mirrors, so you cannot see as much.
Motorcycles have blind spots, just like cars.
Mirrors are never accurate.
Mirrors take your eyes off the road ahead and should not be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. You cannot rely only on mirrors to see what is behind you. Always turn your head to check your blind spots regularly.
